title: “Explain This Person” Courtroom
summary: One fictional behaviour, eight explanations that all fit it. Rate each, request the evidence you want, and find out what separates an explanation that fits from one that predicts.
learningObjectives: Explain what underdetermination means for psychological explanation.
Distinguish an explanation that accommodates a behaviour from one that predicts something distinctive.
Identify what evidence would discriminate between two accounts that both fit.
Distinguish competing explanations from compatible ones.
Calibrate confidence to what the available evidence can support.
privacy: No data collected, stored or transmitted; every calculation runs in the browser tab, and the tool asks nothing about the person using it.
accessibilityNotes: Each explanation is a fieldset whose floated legend carries the full statement, so rating options are never announced orphaned; the floated legend also prevents multi-line legends spilling out of their box. Native radios, checkboxes and buttons throughout. The competition diagram is hidden from assistive technology and paired with a visible table stating every pair's relationship in words; nodes are labelled and supported/undermined states are conveyed by stroke pattern as well as fill. Requirements tick off in a live checklist with '(met)' / '(not yet)' in the text. Changes announced through the shell's polite live region; reduced motion honoured; forced-colours rules provided; usable at 320px and at classroom-projector widths.
readmeTopic: Explanation and underdetermination: why fitting a case is cheap and predicting something distinctive is not
simulationNotes: A fictional case with eight explanations written to be compatible with it, and six pieces of evidence whose findings are stipulated. There is no correct answer and none is stored: the tool has no hidden fact about why the fictional person acted. Explanations are scored on fit and on how much their predictions differ from rivals'; the verdict responds to whether discriminating evidence was requested, whether confidence is proportionate, and whether compatible explanations were kept alive. Distinctiveness is not truth, and the page says so.
